resources.string: "No calibration override applied. Sensor values are used as-is. Use this when the sensor is already factory-calibrated and accurate."

"Per-sensor linear calibration override (slope and offset) computed from your fingerstick entries. Recent entries are weighted higher. Override is applied after the current sensor session start; first 2 hours are skipped as warm-up."
Possible sensor change detected at %1$s. Mark as new sensor?
Log a sensor change to enable calibration.
Fit out of safe range — calibration not applied.
Offset-only calibration applied — sensor range too narrow for slope.
Calibration applied — slope clamped to safe range. Add more entries to relax.
This will invalidate the entry. The fit will be recalculated.

Monotone piecewise-cubic (Fritsch–Carlson) calibration with a single interior knot at 6 mmol/L (108 mg/dL). Corrects S-shaped sensor bias in the clinically critical low range. Falls back to linear calibration when fewer than 4 entries are available or the spline fit is rejected.
Linear fallback active (need %1$d entries for spline)
Linear fallback active (need %1$d entries below 6 mmol/L)
Linear fallback active (need %1$d entries above 6 mmol/L)
Linear fallback active (spline rejected — slope outside safe range)
Linear fallback active (entries too close together for a stable curve)
Linear fallback active (spline rejected — fit would not be monotone)
Additive correction on top of the fit. Use when sensor reads consistently high or low between fingersticks.
